lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The date of birth should be removed.
items.because: It is irrelevant to hiring and creates age-discrimination and privacy concerns.

items.says: Nationality should be removed unless an application requires it.
items.because: It is generally not useful on a North American technical resume.

items.says: Add a target-role title or brief summary beneath the contact information.
items.because: Recruiters currently have to infer which of several adjacent roles you are pursuing.

items.says: Keep the code portfolio URL only if it leads to relevant, accessible evidence.
items.because: An empty, private, or unrelated repository weakens credibility.

items.says: Consider adding directly relevant graduate coursework, research, or specialization.
items.because: The resume does not show what the graduate degree contributes to the target role.

items.says: Make the expected graduation status visually clearer.
items.because: Recruiters may misread the degree as completed.

items.says: Add honors or a relevant capstone only if genuinely strong.
items.because: Extra education detail is worthwhile only if it improves technical positioning.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy, its baseline, and the evaluation set.
items.because: The 35% improvement is hard to judge without knowing the metric and comparison.

items.says: Explain or simplify the dense description of the fine-tuning method.
items.because: Readers may not understand what was trained or which part produced the improvement.

items.says: Clarify the routing layer’s operational purpose and what reviewer disagreement measures.
items.because: The 14% to 6% reduction could describe several different reliability measures.

items.says: Explain the relationship among the specialists, reviewer, and input signals more clearly.
items.because: The current phrasing makes readers reconstruct the system design.

items.says: Give the case count, accuracy-comparison conditions, and latency measurement setting.
items.because: Those conditions make the efficiency result credible.

items.says: Emphasize the system-level efficiency and quality outcome over the GRPO name.
items.because: Recruiters may treat algorithm names as buzzwords.

items.says: State what catching the two regressions prevented, if substantiated.
items.because: The bullet stops short of the business or engineering impact.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned the harness or contributed to a larger system.
items.because: Your level of ownership matters alongside the resume’s other strong ownership claims.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking repeats the method in the earlier fine-tuning bullet.
items.because: It adds no new outcome and makes the resume appear padded.

items.says: If this was a separate experiment, give its separate result.
items.because: A method without a distinct result is weaker than an achievement with measurable impact.

items.says: The diagnostics triage and backlog result appears again in the research-agent project.
items.because: The duplication raises questions about ownership and where the result occurred.

items.says: Make the backlog reduction’s baseline and operational significance unambiguous.
items.because: The eight-week period is given, but what the 68% reduction is measured against is not.

items.says: State what the fourfold memory reduction enabled.
items.because: The reader needs its practical consequence, such as larger batches or fewer out-of-memory failures.

items.says: Specify which GPU-memory measurement fell by 4x.
items.because: A precise technical metric improves credibility.

items.says: Say whether the p95 latency values used comparable workloads and traffic conditions.
items.because: Latency comparisons are meaningful only under comparable conditions.

items.says: Confirm that the build-failure safeguard was enforced in CI.
items.because: It is a strong reliability signal only if it was automated and routinely used.

items.says: The CI bullet shifts from past to present tense.
items.because: The wording reads like an editing error.

items.says: Clarify what a three-day release cycle measures.
items.because: It could mean three days from code completion to release or a cycle reduced to three days.

items.says: Give the previous cycle length or number of releases if available.
items.because: The impact is difficult to assess without a baseline.

items.says: Describe the event-queue migration’s operational result more precisely.
items.because: The outcome should show why the architecture mattered.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the migration across 30 services.
items.because: “Migrated 30 services” implies substantial ownership that should match your role.

items.says: Fix the line-break artifact the review identifies in “dead-letter handling.”
items.because: Source-formatting hyphenation should not appear as an awkward split.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad AI-first adoption claim unless it has a concrete result.
items.because: Its claims about adoption, delivery, and outcomes lack evidence and may sound inflated.

items.says: Explain the context constraint, the 100x comparison, and what capability was preserved.
items.because: “Raw conversation grew 100x” is difficult to interpret.

items.says: State what the context-management design enabled.
items.because: The resulting system behavior matters more than the implementation technique.

items.says: Clarify whether the stress test used representative workloads.
items.because: A technical reviewer may ask about realistic tool calls and message sizes.

items.says: Describe the conditions that caused the deadlocks and lost results.
items.because: That context would make the concurrency fix clearer.

items.says: Define whether 50-way fan-out was a tested limit, production workload, or stress-test setting.
items.because: The number’s meaning depends on its context.

items.says: Quantify the reliability or throughput effect if measured.
items.because: Successful completion or throughput would make the result more compelling.

items.says: Specify what integrating the eight metrics involved.
items.because: “Integrated” is broad and does not show what you built.

items.says: Link the open-source contribution if the repository is accessible.
items.because: Reviewers can verify the contribution only if they can find it.

items.says: Explain what the Kendall correlation demonstrates operationally.
items.because: Many readers will not know whether it means the evaluator ranked degradation or detected quality loss.

items.says: Clarify the unit of analysis and source of the 400-plus trials.
items.because: Readers may want to know whether the reports were synthetic, human-authored, or production-like.

items.says: The diagnostics triage result duplicates the Mobility Systems Company achievement.
items.because: Counting what appears to be one accomplishment twice creates a credibility problem.

items.says: If this was independent work, distinguish its ownership, data, setting, or result.
items.because: Otherwise the project and professional work appear to be the same achievement.

items.says: Separate programming languages from development tools if the skills list grows.
items.because: Languages, version control, and infrastructure tools signal different capabilities.

items.says: Expand the skills section to reflect demonstrated evaluation and systems capabilities.
items.because: It underrepresents the strongest technical themes in the experience bullets.

items.says: Prioritize the most relevant bullets within each role.
items.because: Recruiters often read only the first one or two bullets under a position.

items.says: Choose a dominant technical story across ML engineering, agent infrastructure, evaluation, and software engineering.
items.because: Without prioritization, the resume supports several interpretations but leaves the target unclear.

items.says: Check whether other evaluation and reliability claims describe overlapping work.
items.because: Duplicate content reduces perceived breadth and can make metrics look counted more than once.

items.says: Check formatting, terminology, and capitalization consistency.
items.because: The review flags visual and line-break artifacts as needing attention.
